faq: What can I build with the Framer CMS?
Blogs, case study libraries, team pages, job boards, resource libraries and simple directories. We recommend a structure based on the content you plan to publish.
Is there a limit on CMS items?
Framer sets item limits per plan, and they change over time. We check the current limits against your plan before building and tell you if you need a higher one.
Can you import my existing posts?
Yes. We import from a spreadsheet, a WordPress export or by hand, and tidy images and headings. We confirm the source and format with you before we start.
Framer does not offer public submission by default. We can connect a form to a spreadsheet or tool so you review submissions first, and add the approved ones to the CMS.

desc:
A Framer CMS blog and directory build turns a pile of repeating content into a tidy system you can edit without touching the layout. Ecom Swift LLC designs the fields, list pages and detail templates for blogs, case studies, team pages, job boards and directories in your own Framer project.

## What is the Framer CMS?

The Framer CMS is the built-in content manager that stores lists of items, such as posts or projects, in collections. Each collection has fields, like title, image, category and body text. You design one template for the list page and one for the detail page, and Framer fills them from the entries.

That means a new blog post is a form to fill in, not a page to design. The work is in setting up the fields and templates well, because everything you add later depends on them.

## Why the structure matters more than the design

A CMS built in a hurry looks fine on day one and hurts on day sixty. Fields are missing, so editors paste formatting into the body. Categories are typed by hand and spelled three ways. Images arrive in different shapes and break the grid. Every new entry needs a developer to fix it.

A well-planned collection prevents this. Fields are named for what they hold, images have a fixed role, categories come from a single list, and the template handles the rest. You add content in minutes and the page looks right every time.

## How a good CMS helps your site perform

Fresh, well-organized content gives search engines and visitors more to find and read. A blog with clear categories and related posts keeps readers moving from one article to the next. A case study list lets prospects find work like theirs. A directory with filters lets people narrow a long list to the few entries they care about.

There is a practical benefit too. When publishing is easy, it happens more often. Teams that can add an entry without waiting for a designer tend to keep their sites current, and a current site gives visitors more reason to trust it.

## What a well-built Framer CMS includes

- Collections with fields chosen for the content type, such as summary, cover image, author, date and category.
- A list page that shows entries in a clean grid or list, with consistent card sizes.
- A detail page template with a readable body, headings, images and a clear next step.
- Categories or tags that come from one controlled list.
- Filters or a search box where the list is long enough to need them.
- Related items on detail pages, so readers keep moving.
- Page titles and descriptions generated from fields, so each entry is search ready.
- Author or team pages pulled from the CMS where they fit.
- A sitemap and feed that include the new entries.
- A short guide showing how to add, edit and publish an entry.

## How we build it

We start with the content itself. You tell us what you publish and how you want people to find it, and we sketch the fields and the page layout before touching the project. Then we create the collections, design the list and detail templates to match your brand, and test them with sample entries of different lengths.

The Basic package covers one collection with its list and detail pages and a first batch of entries. Standard adds a second collection, filters, related items and a larger import. Premium covers linked collections, a search box with several filters, author or team pages, a bigger import, a feed and sitemap check, and a period of fixes after launch.

If you have existing content in a spreadsheet or on another site, we bring it in rather than asking you to retype it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide the fields before the design, because fields shape the templates.
- Use one image ratio per collection.
- Keep category names short and consistent.
- Write summaries so list cards read well.
- Add a few real entries early to test the layout.

**Avoid:**
- Putting formatting instructions inside the body text.
- Creating a collection for something that is only three static items.
- Adding filters that nobody will use.
- Leaving entry titles vague, since they become page titles.
- Building directory-style features on a list that has only a handful of items.

## Who this is for

A consultant who wants a blog and a set of case studies that anyone on the team can update will get value from this. So will an agency that needs a team page and a job board managed from one place. A local organization building a directory of members, venues or resources is another good fit, especially when the list will keep growing.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of what you publish, a few example entries, and any existing content in a document, spreadsheet or old site address. Share your logo, colors and fonts if the project does not already have them. Invite us to your Framer project as a collaborator, so we work in your own account. We never need your password.

Tell us if visitors should be able to submit entries. We will explain what the CMS can and cannot do for that before we start.
